Project Description:
National Large Solar telescope is a 2 m class large sized solar telescope project. Once, it is established near the Pangong Tso near Merak village in Leh, Ladakh, it will be the largest solar telescope in Asia. The 2-m class telescope can able to resolve 50 km sized magnetic features on the Sun. This will help the solar astronomers to understand the origin, evolution and submergence of the solar large scale magnetic fields. 

The support facility for the National Large Solar Telescope project need to be build about 1 km away from the main telescope land. There, the optics laboratory, mechanical and electronic laboratory is planned to be built. One astronomy museum will be made and it will be open for the public.  For this purpose, the Indian Institute of Astrophysics requires 5 Acres of land near the village to establish support facilities.

Project Description: Ground-based gamma-ray astronomy using Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes(IACTs) has advanced over the last three decades, establishing VHE gamma-ray studies as a vital branch of multi-messenger astronomy.The Major Atmospheric Cherenkov Experiment (MACE) at Hanle has contributed significantly as a single telescope, but it faces limitations in background rejection and in angular and energy resolution. These challenges can be overcome by stereoscopic observations, where two or more IACTs observe the same air shower. The proposed Stereo MACE System (SMS) with two identical telescopes, will enhance sensitivity, lower energy threshold, and provide superior reconstruction accuracy. The project will lead to socio economic development of the region and inspire students nationwide. International teams are seeking collaborations with MACE. SMS will boost AtmaNirbhar Bharat by developing indigenous optics and camera electronics,positioning India at the forefront of high-energy astrophysics.

Project Description:
The existing Leh–Chalunka Road from Km 180.00 to Km 192.600 is presently built to CL-9 specifications, which are inadequate for the movement of heavy military vehicles and increasing traffic. This strategic road connects the Indus Valley, Shyok Valley, and forward areas towards Turtuk and serves as a vital route for operational, administrative, and civilian movement.

The proposed project under 54 RCC / HQ 16 BRTF / Project Vijayak aims to upgrade this stretch to NHDL specifications, improving pavement strength, carriageway width, and overall road safety. The upgradation will ensure faster and safer movement of defence forces, enhance logistical support to forward areas, and provide improved connectivity for the local population.
